merger_name: Australian Venue Co – assets of The Breakwater, Hillarys and Print Hall, Perth

anzsic_codes.name: Amusement and Other Recreational Activities n.e.c.

merger_description:
AVC Operations Pty Limited (**AVC**), a subsidiary of Australian Venue Co. Holdings Ltd, proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets of two licensed venues located in Western Australia, being The Breakwater, Hillarys, and Print Hall, Perth, from Wintime Nominees Pty Ltd and Sunliner Holdings Pty Ltd respectively (the **Acquisition**). The Acquisition includes the assignment of the lease for each venue. The business assets of these venues are currently owned and operated by each respective vendor as part of the Night Owl Group.

AVC operates over 200 licensed venues throughout Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars, clubs and licensed restaurants. AVC's venues are individually branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metro areas, offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and gaming facilities. AVC’s venues in the Perth CBD and Northbridge area include Durty Nelly’s Irish Pub, The Aviary, The Generous Squire, The Globe, Lil’s Rooftop & Bar, Market Grounds, An Sibin and The Court.

The Breakwater is a licensed venue located at 203/58 Southside Drive, Hillarys WA. The venue is a waterfront destination featuring multiple bars, a restaurant, entertainment facilities (including bowling and shuffleboard) and function rooms.

Print Hall is a multi-level licensed venue located at Brookfield Place, 125 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA. The venue is a heritage-listed entertainment precinct featuring multiple bars, a cellar wine bar, branded/themed restaurants and a rooftop terrace.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information regarding The
Breakwater and Print Hall, and AVC’s other venues in Perth, Western
Australia.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The aggregation in retail hospitality venues within the central
Perth local area arising from the Acquisition, including both
AVC’s previous acquisitions over the last three years and AVC’s
acquisition of Molly’s Highgate and Molly’s Victoria Park (which
the ACCC determined, on the same date as this Determination,
may be put into effect), is material.
• However, AVC would continue to face competition from
alternative retail hospitality venues in the local area surrounding
Print Hall and the local area surrounding The Breakwater.
